about.label: Approach
body: I am a frontend developer at InspireIT in Ankara. Alongside it I am finishing a management information systems degree at İstanbul University.

Most of what I do is the unglamorous half of frontend: taking something that already works and making it easier to change. Splitting a page into parts that stand on their own. Removing what is on screen until what matters is obvious.
I am early in this. Everything listed here is work I actually did, described as it is.

items.name: Interfaces
items.what: A web interface built from scratch: a marketing site, a product front end, a dashboard.
items.how: Components that stand on their own, content kept in data rather than repeated markup, real routes and real HTML underneath.
items.when: You have a design or a clear idea and need it to exist in a browser, on every screen size, without a framework fight later.
items.honesty: Design is not what I sell. Give me a design, or let me keep it simple.

items.name: Rework
items.what: Something that already works but is slow, fragile or hard to change.
items.how: Measure first, then split the page into parts, remove what is not needed, and fix what the numbers point at.
items.when: Every change takes five edits, the page feels heavy on a phone, or nobody dares to touch the old code.
items.stack: Lighthouse, Web Vitals, profiling, accessibility audits
items.honesty: The unglamorous half of frontend. It is most of what I do.

items.name: Motion
items.what: Scroll-driven and pointer-driven pages: layered heroes, pinned scenes, video the wheel controls.
items.how: Transform and opacity only, a static composition that works with no motion at all, verified frame by frame on desktop and phone.
items.when: You want a page that feels like an experience rather than a document, and you want it to stay fast.
items.stack: GSAP ScrollTrigger, Lenis, CSS scroll-driven animation
items.honesty: This site is the sample. Everything on it is built this way.
